elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section 5.4: "IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL..." IBM is Customer; the right is unconditional and covers the Agreement (the element is disjunctive, so Agreement-level coverage suffices). The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" reflects the pre-redline document (which supports the 'missing' classification); the rendered operative text plainly contains the new right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL" — exactly 30 days, in writing, no additional conditions or Vendor consent.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination" — express pro rata basis (not merely a post-termination-period refund), payable by Vendor (MSL).

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 5.0 grants termination rights only "by either Party for cause as follows", and the redline adds a convenience right for IBM only. Section 4.0's six (6) months' notice operates on the automatic twelve-month renewal (natural-term non-renewal, assessed under RENEWAL, not T4C), and SOW 6.1 is a Customer-side Purchase Order cancellation right. No mid-term MSL convenience exit exists.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause uses thirty (30) days, which is below the 60–90 day fallback band. To sit at the fallback the operative notice period would have to be changed to 60–90 days; as drafted the proposal is a preferred-level, not fallback-level, ask.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Conditional element that does not apply: the redline imposes no early-termination fee or cancellation charge on IBM for Agreement-level convenience termination (it creates a refund obligation running to IBM), and no retained clause attaches a termination penalty to the new Section 5.4. SOW 6.1's cost-reimbursement mechanic is a Purchase Order cancellation term left untouched.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Vendor has no convenience right at all: Section 5.0 confines termination to cause and the redline adds convenience rights for IBM only, which is a fortiori stronger than 'end of term only'. Residual note: Section 4.0's six-month notice is renewal-scoped rather than a mid-term MSL convenience exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Conditional element that does not apply because MSL has no convenience termination right; the only MSL notice mechanic (Section 4.0 non-renewal) requires six (6) months, well in excess of 90 days.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted Section 5.4 supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and the absence of any MSL mid-term convenience right is already true on the face of Section 5.0.

Fallback is not independently satisfied (30 days sits outside the 60–90 day band), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is complete; the margin comment correctly reserves 60–90 days as a concession without putting it in operative text.

Minimal: one concise insertion for a missing clause, no deletions, nothing struck from Section 4.0, 5.1–5.3, SOW 6.1 or the Parts pricing paragraph, and no extras (no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added damages or procedure). Omitting the model language's 'in whole or in part' is correct here since no Order Form/partial-termination structure is selected.

Intent preserved: Section 4.0's cross-reference to 'unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0' still resolves because the new right is placed inside Section 5.0; no defined term is left dangling and the renewal, for-cause and Purchase Order mechanics survive unchanged.

Drafting hardening (optional, not a defect): Section 5.1's retained preamble 'Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows' is permissive rather than exclusive, so it does not contradict Section 5.4; if MSL argues it is exclusive, open Section 5.4 with 'Notwithstanding Section 5.1,' rather than deleting or rewriting Section 5.1.
